advisories.title: 'post-commit' is new vocabulary and is not grounded against the golden's own committed-Run boundary
advisories.detail: The phrase 'post-commit' appears three times in v12 and zero times in v11, so it enters the contract here. Meanwhile /requiredOutputFailure/committedRunBoundary — unchanged — says the golden also covers the case with no committed Run: 'Commands with no committed Run (help/version and any other) do not gain a Run to satisfy this golden.' So the required serialization operation is not inherently post-commit, and calling it 'the existing post-commit required serialization operation' narrows it without saying why the narrowing holds here.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: For this surface the narrowing is almost certainly right and merely unstated: D-002 advertises SARIF for analyze only, and analyze commits a Run, so a SARIF native-location validation is post-commit in every case it can arise. The sentence also carries its own disclaimer that no new D9 code or exit is minted, which I verified. Nothing false follows and no recipe is minted — this is a grounding gap, not an overreach.
advisories.suggestedFix: One clause noting that the SARIF projection surface is analyze-only and therefore always post-commit, or drop the qualifier and say 'inside the existing required serialization operation'.

verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories. The dispatch gate was 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: All three claimed repairs are real and I verified each against the bytes rather than the claim. The claude2v10 pin is restored to the exact specification both lanes gave, including the distinction Codex asked for between a not-folded advisory and an external non-subject one. The cardinality members are now expressed over a single declared count domain, and the golden-side phrasing that both lanes objected to is gone — I confirmed it is present in v11 and absent in v12. The multiple-primary branch is classified into the existing post-commit required serialization operation and fails under a golden I checked exists: 'machine-output-serialization-failed', pre-existing at an unchanged /requiredOutputFailure, already disclaiming any new D9 code or exit. No D9 recipe is minted, no RunId or artifact-ref recipe is minted, G17 is refused in all eleven places it appears, and the roster holds at twenty paths including the scope qualifier it puts on /machineSurface. One thing fails. My own v11 advisory ADV-SPC-V11-01 was folded by this successor's cardinality rewrite and is recorded in neither column — the string occurs twice in the whole document, once on the verdict record this successor added and once in a namespace list that is not a disposition. Its two siblings on that same new record are correctly booked not folded, so the successor plainly holds itself to the invariant and missed the one item its own repair satisfied. One honestyRepairsFromV11 line closes it.
bindsTo: START and END bytes 51d5ecf1741079e5c2dbda253f8a2beccb8e8a8491f6f91b1f5d92203803edbb — identical at both ends. Measured with Python hashlib at both ends; the subject did not move during review and was not edited by me.
coordinatorNote: REJECT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-122 stays OPEN at file 08 line 304. Nothing here mints a D-096 (A) grant, a RunId or Finding recipe, or a D9 code; G17 is not resurrected; no implementation is authorized. This is a REJECT on a single missing ledger line and the proportion matters: the substantive repair work this round is sound, and the two hardest things to get right — binding the multiple-primary failure to an existing golden without minting a D9 code, and keeping one count domain across cardinality and validation — are both done correctly. Add one honestyRepairsFromV11 entry recording ADV-SPC-V11-01 as folded by the SARIFV11-S2 rewrite and, on my measurement, this artifact carries zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. I would fold both advisories into the same edit rather than spend another round: one clause admitting CODEX-V<n>-* as a historical alias, which would also let the ledger be swept mechanically instead of by hand, and one clause grounding 'post-commit' in the analyze-only scope of the SARIF surface. Two scope facts. HEAD advanced to 8daa2e6 (D-110) during this review; the subject did not move, I re-verified every pin afterwards, and the artifact's own remeasurement is correct for the HEAD the dispatch named. And this prompt's read set did not include the v5 through v10 verdicts, so for findings recorded from those rounds I checked digests and internal accounting only and take no position on whether they are substantively satisfied.
